event.title: Free Workflow Task slots across Workers
event.why: Schedule-to-start is how long a task waits for a Worker to start it. A Worker only polls when it can reserve a free Workflow Task slot, so if every Worker had used all its slots, tasks would wait — the one cause more Workers would fix. This single query confirms or rules that out.

event.title: Failed Workflow Task polls
event.why: A signal flood competes with polls for Frontend rate-limit capacity: Signals are admitted at a higher priority and reserve tokens polls depend on. Rejected polls make Workers back off while slots stay free. Poll failures seen by the Workers show whether that happened.

event.title: Task Queue backlog, add and dispatch rates
event.why: With Worker capacity free and polls not throttled, the question is where the wait accrues. DescribeTaskQueue reports Matching's backlog, the rates tasks are added and dispatched, and the effective dispatch rate limit, which together locate the constraint in Matching or before it. It also lists the Workers that polled in the last 5 minutes, which settles whether any did.

collect.label: DescribeTaskQueue with statistics, through grpcurl, captured during the incident — point it at a Frontend, which answers gRPC reflection, so grpcurl needs no proto files; -emit-defaults keeps zero rates and an empty poller list, which protobuf JSON leaves out; with TLS, use -cacert, -cert and -key instead of -plaintext; record when you captured it

If you cannot run grpcurl: the Temporal CLI's description, as JSON, without the rate limit — CLI 1.7.0 to 1.9.1 print the backlog, rates and pollers but not the effective rate limit, and describe only the unversioned queue, or the default Build ID's, so with versioned Workers use grpcurl; record when you captured it

event.title: Task Queue partition configuration
event.why: The effective dispatch limit is the per-partition limit multiplied by the read partitions. The partition settings in effect for order-fulfillment show where the limit comes from, and whether tasks are written to partitions no poller reads.

subject.description: Schedule-to-start with the dispatch limit alone

notes.text: Simulated by tempdes 22b8dc9 with seed 1: one Task Queue whose only constraint is its dispatch limit, for the 15-minute incident window. Calibrated on E4, E5: 2,112 Workflow Tasks a second added against a limit of 2,000 a second, over 2 read partitions.
Both rates were divided by 20 to keep the run small. Their ratio, which sets the wait, is unchanged.
Schedule-to-start reached 40.6 s in the simulation, 1.35× the 30 s observed.

tempdes models Temporal 1.31.0 on EKS, with Workers that follow the Go SDK. A run that reproduces the latency is consistent with the cause, not proof of it, so it can support or weaken the hypothesis but never settle it.
